name: Separator
summary: A rule between things. Horizontal or vertical, one hairline in the border colour — the thing a sidebar uses between sections and a toolbar uses between groups.

a11y.apg: No pattern is needed and that is the point: a native <hr> already carries role="separator" implicitly, so writing the role would be redundant ARIA — and the APG's own warning is that no ARIA beats bad ARIA. The separator role defaults to horizontal orientation, so aria-orientation is emitted ONLY when the separator is vertical. There is no keyboard interaction: a separator is not focusable and never was.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Horizontal is a full-width hairline; vertical is a 1px column that stretches to the tallest sibling, with a floor so it cannot measure zero inside a flex row. BEHAVIOURAL and not visual: the resolved value goes to the engine, which publishes data-orientation and, in the vertical case, aria-orientation — the horizontal one is role="separator"'s implicit default and announcing it would be noise. This is why the component is client-side: an attribute cannot come from a CSS class.

props.name: spacing
props.description: The space on both sides of the line (C-04), in the same three steps as the layout primitives' gap (ADR-0051). On a vertical separator the space goes to the sides.

notes: It is pure markup and ships NO JavaScript. The engine already in use (Base UI) HAS a Separator, and it was deliberately not used: it is marked 'use client', it calls a hook, and all it produces is role="separator" plus aria-orientation — two attributes. Importing it would drag this module across the server/client boundary, which is the defect ADR-0026 records (Card cost 118.5 KB crossing it). This is the rare case where "if the engine delivers it, we do not write it" loses to the boundary.

It draws with `background` on a 1px box, not with `border`: the thickness then does not depend on which border side someone wrote, and one class serves both orientations. The browser's own <hr> margin and border are zeroed — otherwise the rule arrives with spacing nobody asked for.

NOT included, and on purpose: the three separator tones HeroUI carries (secondary/tertiary), because this system has one --border and inventing a tone scale here would be copying their token system; and the separator WITH A LABEL in the middle ("or", a date inside a conversation), which is a different structure since an <hr> cannot carry text. That one is the next step if anybody needs it.
Inside a Toolbar use ToolbarSeparator, not this one: the toolbar's separator takes part in the roving tabindex the engine manages. Base UI splits the two for the same reason.
